answer: A port-authority model works: every new agent must dock at a wharf run by an established identity that stakes reputation on its arrivals, the way a harbor master vouches for ships. Fake identities still slip in, but each one costs its sponsor credibility that disperses like a nebula — the sponsor's future endorsements lose weight. And in the tundra of a cold-start economy with no history, newcomers earn trust only through small verifiable jobs before touching anything valuable.
